record.paper_title: Ramsey theory of homogeneous structures: current trends and open problems
record.original_question: For which infinite structures S does every finite substructure A have a finite big Ramsey degree? Equivalently, for each finite A contained in S, is there a positive integer T such that every finite coloring of the copies of A in S admits an isomorphic subcopy S' of S in which the copies of A use at most T colors; when such T exists, the least possible T is the big Ramsey degree T(A).

evidence.quote: Question 1.3. For which infinite structures S is there a Ramsey-analogue in the following sense: Let A be a finite substructure of S. Is there a positive integer T such that for any coloring of the copies of A into finitely many colors, there is a subcopy S′ of S in which there are no more than T many colors for the copies of A?
The least such integer T , when it exists, is denoted T (A) and called the big Ramsey degree of A in S

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be an infinite (typically countable, relational) structure. For a finite substructure $A \subseteq S$, write $\binom{S}{A}$ for the set of isomorphic copies of $A$ inside $S$. The big Ramsey degree of $A$ in $S$, denoted $T(A,S)$, is defined as the least positive integer $T$ such that for every finite coloring $c:\binom{S}{A}\to k$ (with $k<\infty$), there exists an isomorphic copy $S' \subseteq S$ of $S$ such that the restriction of $c$ to $\binom{S'}{A}$ uses at most $T$ colors; if no such $T$ exists, set $T(A,S)=\infty$.

Characterize the infinite structures $S$ with the property that $T(A,S)<\infty$ for every finite substructure $A$ of $S$. Equivalently, determine for which infinite structures $S$ every finite substructure $A\subseteq S$ admits a positive integer $T$ such that any finite coloring of the copies of $A$ in $S$ can be reduced, on some isomorphic subcopy $S'$ of $S$, to at most $T$ colors.
artifact.category_tag: Big Ramsey degrees of homogeneous structures
artifact.status_search_result: The general classification problem of which infinite structures have all finite big Ramsey degrees remains open. Substantial recent progress has been achieved for specific classes (e.g., binary free amalgamation classes with forbidden irreducible substructures, and the universal homogeneous 3-uniform hypergraph, established in 2021–2022), and a 2024 survey on big Ramsey structures consolidates the framework but explicitly leaves the general characterization, and related questions such as the existence of big Ramsey structures, as open.

status_evidence.title: A survey on big Ramsey structures
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys big Ramsey structures, lists open problems including whether every homogeneous structure with finite big Ramsey degrees admits a big Ramsey structure.
status_evidence.claim: The general theory and classification of structures with finite big Ramsey degrees is an active area with major problems still open as of 2024.

status_evidence.title: Big Ramsey Degrees of 3-Uniform Hypergraphs Are Finite
status_evidence.snippet: First example outside binary languages where finite big Ramsey degrees are established.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress: finiteness established for new specific homogeneous structures, but the general question is not resolved.

status_evidence.title: On big Ramsey degrees for binary free amalgamation classes
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes finite big Ramsey degrees for a wide class of binary free amalgamation classes.
status_evidence.claim: Significant partial progress but does not give a full characterization.
